items.title: A dense closable gradient for a genuine Gibbs measure

source.anchor: section2.5 weighted Sobolev construction; direct Euclidean prerequisite
source.attribution: Kolesnikov and Milman background; Chen, Chewi, Lu and Zhang PBPS consumer; ASTIS expanded mathematical proof.

items.statement: Section2.5 of Kolesnikov-Milman describes weighted H1 and H10 by completing smooth test functions in the graph norm on its compact weighted manifold. The selected ASTIS analytic prerequisite is a directly proved Euclidean full-space construction, not that source spectral conclusion: for d>=1, C1 W with integrable exp(-W), the graph of smooth compact f and their genuine gradients determines a densely defined closable scalar-to-vector L2 operator under the normalized Gibbs measure. Its graph closure remains single-valued. This explicit construction is needed before a weighted resolvent route to PBPS conditional Poincare. No manifold boundary theorem or D*D operator-core assertion is included.
assumptions: Selected full-space prerequisite: d>=1, W:R^d->R C1 and exp(-W) integrable, actual normalized Gibbs measure and smooth compact tests.
The background discussion is on compact weighted manifolds with smoother potential; full-space construction and weaker C1 regularity are explicit scope changes, not silent specialization.

items.title: The actual conditional PBPS gradient is densely defined and closable

source.attribution: Kolesnikov and Milman background; Chen, Chewi, Lu and Zhang PBPS consumer; ASTIS expanded mathematical proof.

items.statement: PBPS Appendix C.1 uses conditional Poincare for the actual reflected Gibbs-Gaussian conditional law. The selected ASTIS prerequisite constructs the actual weighted gradient domain and closure on that law: with W_y(u)=V((y+u)/2)+norm(u-y)^2/(8eta), S_y is normalized exp(-W_y) volume, and the smooth compact gradient graph in L2(S_y) is densely defined and closable. The original source PI/variance application is not proved by this prerequisite. Kernels, normalization and potential regularity must be those of the actual augmentation.
assumptions: Paper setting: Euclidean d>=1, V C2, 0<alpha<=beta, genuine alpha/beta Hessian bounds, eta>0 and beta eta<=1.
The actual joint law is (X,X+sqrt(eta)Z) with independent Gibbs X and standard Gaussian Z; the reflected conditional law is S_y.
